title: Validate the user problem and evidence behind deliver linked screen and diagram editing
summary: Validate the target user, context, unmet need, baseline, and decision-changing evidence for `open repository-backed design truth, place screens and diagram objects, select and transform them, connect flows, inspect source context, and save`.
acceptance_criteria: State the primary user or operator, job, context, and intended value for `internal visual product, design, diagram, and proposal workspace`.

Frame the flagship journey as a testable problem statement: open repository-backed design truth, place screens and diagram objects, select and transform them, connect flows, inspect source context, and save.
Separate known facts, repository evidence, assumptions, preferences, hypotheses, and unresolved questions.
Define the smallest set of research questions that can change product or investment decisions.
Define who should and should not participate, including internal dogfood users where the product is personal or operational.
Use purposive recruitment rather than claiming statistical representation from a convenience sample.
Define consent, recording, retention, redaction, and withdrawal before collecting research evidence.
Avoid collecting credentials, full private archives, health details, financial records, customer data, or media unless strictly required and separately approved.
Define the current baseline using product, support, analytics, performance, and qualitative evidence already owned by the repository.
Review comparable products only to understand expectations and gaps, not to copy protected assets or dark patterns.
Map research questions to product charter, critical journey, assurance claim, and decision ticket.
Define success, failure, inconclusive, blocked, and not-enough-evidence outcomes.
Define how conflicting feedback will be recorded without averaging away meaningful differences.
Define how accessibility, localization, device, experience level, and usage context affect the study.
Pilot the research script or dogfood task before inviting broader participants.
Keep moderator prompts neutral and avoid leading users toward the intended design.
Record observed behavior separately from participant interpretation and researcher inference.
Link every insight to exact evidence, date, product version, and limitation.
Produce proposed findings rather than automatic implementation tickets.
Define expiry or revalidation triggers when the product or target user changes.
Update repository-owned research and product documentation without changing source behavior.
Finish the planning and tooling slice with zero app-owned warnings.

agent_notes: Portfolio Human Validation & Product Launch Wave 13.
Non-scope: do not release, deploy, sign, publish, enable billing or ads, operate hardware, write NAS data, migrate users, merge products, or create future game repositories.
Alternative considered and rejected: relying on internal confidence, green builds, or download counts without observed user or operator value would create false product certainty.
Research, telemetry, and feedback must remain privacy-safe, versioned, and optional where the product role requires it.

Final Wave 14 validity review: `valid-after-sudoku`; publication `publish-as-proposed-backlog`; implementation sequence `after-sudoku`. Human validation remains valuable after the product implementation prerequisites and Sudoku priority.
